My name is on this small piece of land here in Balaka, and maize is what feeds my family. I will try to get the subsidy fertilizer if I can, and I save some goat manure from home to mix in the planting holes because chemical alone is too expensive for me. I plant hybrid seed when I can afford it from the agro-dealer in town, and I intercrop with pigeon peas to help the soil and give us another food. Rains have been poor these last seasons so I cannot irrigate — I just pray the rains come on time and weed the field myself with my wife and older children.
